description: Calculate the adsorption energy of CO on the Pt(111) surface at the top site.
user_prompt: Calculate the adsorption energy of CO on the Pt(111) surface (FCC, Fm-3m) at the top site. Report the final adsorption energy Eads (in eV), defined as Eads = E(slab+CO) - E(slab) - E(CO).

references: Hammer, Morikawa & Norskov, Phys. Rev. Lett. 76, 2141 (1996)
Feibelman, Hammer, Norskov, Wagner, Scheffler, Stumpf, Watwe & Dumesic, J. Phys. Chem. B 105, 4018 (2001)
method.modeling: Pt(111) slab with at least 4 layers, vacuum >= 15 Angstrom, and a 3x3x1 or larger surface supercell; adsorb CO C-down on a top Pt atom. Reference the adsorption energy to the clean Pt(111) slab plus gas-phase CO.
method.rationale: Value is the electronic adsorption energy for top-site CO on Pt(111), written in the negative Eads convention used by this benchmark. The final state is C-down CO bound to an atop Pt atom; Feibelman et al. 2001 documents that semilocal DFT can favor the fcc hollow site, so a hollow-site relaxation is not the target for this prompt. The +/-0.20 eV absolute tolerance covers coverage, k-mesh, slab-thickness, and PBE/PW91 implementation differences.
